keyFindings.description: A fourth verdict-less return, and this round's own comment calls it a verdict. documentChanged's in-flight-write guard returns false after dueRooms has already spent that room's window, and nothing re-arms it; the enumeration added at :234-243 lists 'a write of this process in flight' among the verdicts that have done the window's work. Of the three things hasWriteInFlight reports (roomstate.go), two have a rescue: a browser append from a behind room is refused by the gate and fails the room, and a settlement retries three times two seconds apart and fails it. The third does not: a live write forks cold - coldFork sets forkCursor nil precisely so it is not gated - and a live write that appends nothing (applyLive returning no changes, a mutate error, a rolled-back operation) sends no notification at all, so nothing comes back for that room. The end state is the one rounds 2 and 4 each blocked on, reached through a fourth door, and a no-op API write is at least as common as the failing pool read the three existing arms were built against. Fix: armRetry on that path too - the next wake reaches a verdict cheaply by then - or, if it is to stay a verdict, name the three rescues in the comment and say which one the guarantee rests on. Both thermonuclear passes found this independently.

The re-arm is unbounded in duration, and a permanently armed wake retires the idle ping. armRetry re-arms at a fixed now+staleRoomEvictInterval with no attempt count and no ceiling, so a room whose head read or Evict keeps failing is re-armed every two seconds with no notification arriving at all. wakeIn then stays at about two seconds, which is below DefaultListenIdle, so waitFor returns (wake, true) every round and listen never reaches the ping - the round trip the listener's own comment calls the only thing that finds a half-open connection, since WaitForNotification on a half-open socket returns deadline-exceeded rather than an error and pgx keeps such a connection open. The evictor then stops hearing every other document's notification with nothing logged and nothing failed. This could not happen before this round: the deferred set drained whenever notifications stopped, which is exactly the reasoning the previous round's audit relied on. Fix: back the re-arm off per consecutive no-verdict attempt to a ceiling at or above ListenIdle, which restores the ping for free through waitFor's existing wake >= idle branch - pglisten already owns that shape in Backoff - or make the ping fire on the last proven round trip rather than on the last wait's length.

Stream.CloseAll still says 'Test-only' and now has a production caller: eventStreamRelay.resetCursor calls it on every detected event-log reset, which that function documents as an intended production path. Broker.CloseAll's note is still right; this one misdirects the next reader of the overflow and close path.

Register's returned wait never returns for a server built without Deps.Lifetime, since register mounts the relay on s.lifetime(), which is context.Background() then, and waitBackground waits on it unconditionally where the old waitDelivery returned at once. Round 5 answered this with a doc comment rather than a no-op wait. Defensible, since no in-tree caller is affected, but a hang is not an error and the PR body does not name it; it is in the risk list now.

Service.Evict ignores its context entirely and runs on the listener's goroutine from documentChanged; its flush takes the document's advisory lock through the pool with no bound, so one document whose lock is held by a long transaction stalls every other room's eviction and the listener's redial with it. The evictor's type comment accepts a wait of this kind, but it is written about a bounded read rather than an unbounded close.

Two clock-origin facts in the new rows' comments, neither a defect. The gap is measured from a stamp taken on the test's side of the socket close, which is later than the server's own recordEviction, so it under-reads the true elapsed window: the assertion is permissive rather than conservative, the opposite of what its comment claims it cannot do - true only against the other placement it compares itself with. And requireTheRoomClosed's budget starts when the helper is called rather than at wrote, so the effective bound is four seconds plus the write's own duration, while the 6.018 s rescue figure it is set against was taken from wrote. The margin holds at the measured 91-164 ms, but the two numbers are not on one clock origin.
